To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the isovector orbital contribution is the dominant one in the $M1$ strength in the ${}^{3}\overline{p}$H system.

(i) the isovector orbital contribution is found to dominate the isovector M1 strength in the $T = 1/2$ $^{27}$Al and $^{27}$Si mirror nuclei, and (ii) the isoscalar orbital contribution is found not to be negligible.

we have determined the isoscalar, the isovector, the spin, and the orbital contributions to the M1 matrix elements in the T=1/2 mirror nuclei 27Al and 27Si, and that we have shown that shell model calculations reproduce the experimental results.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the separation of the isoscalar, orbital and isovector, spin components of the $M1$ operator.
the determination of the isoscalar, orbital, isovector and spin contributions in the M1 transitions of the $^{27}\mathrm{\mathrm{Al}}$ and $^{27}\,\mathrm{Si}$ mirror nuclei.
the study of the isovectors, isoscalars, spin, and orbital $M1$ transition matrix elements in mirror nuclei.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the isovector orbital component dominates the isovector $1^{+}$ transitions in the $T = 1/2$ nuclei.
the isovector $T=1$ $M1$ transitions are dominated by the spin component.

the isoscalar $M1$ component is the dominant contribution to $M1$ transitions in the $T$=1/2 mirror nuclei, but that the isovector $T=1$ component is also important and that the isovectors $T=1,2$ and $T=0$ are of similar size.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the isoscalar $M1$ strength is found to be about $10-20$\% of the isovectors $M1$ and $GT$ strength.
the $M1$ transitions in the mirror nuclei ${}^27\text{Si}$ and ${}^27 \text{Al}$ are dominated by the orbital component.
the experimental results are in good agreement with the shell model predictions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the orbital and spin components are not equal in the $T = 1/2$ nuclei.
the orbital contribution to the M1 strength is much larger than the spin component.
the isoscalar $M1$ component is the dominant component of the $M1$ transition in the $T = 1/2$ mirrors.
